correctness.rationale: The marked-Poisson first-arrival identity is exact; its Brownian killed-hitting transform gives success probability exp(-sqrt b) and finite conditional delay. A uniform endpoint Laplace expansion at the smaller root phi_c(h)=1 produces the L^(-5/2) prefactor and exact reflected-Gumbel centering for all fixed c<1. A simple uniform delay bound proves exponential limits for c>=1 and in the finite critical window. The 92-check standalone deterministic program corroborates formulas without substituting for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Known exact arrival identities, killed-hitting transforms, fast-immigration and fixed-mortality results are explicitly excluded. The assessed result is the sharp jointly moving mortality/recruitment cutoff with c-dependent reflected-Gumbel normalization and critical window. Searches and inspected material did not establish logical coverage; unavailable full texts and possible general uniform-arrival theorems remain non-negligible risks, with no independent novelty certification.
residual_risks: The full texts of arXiv:2610.08022, arXiv:2606.16025 and arXiv:2508.14202 could not all be inspected, so an implicit general-arrival theorem may cover parts of the claim.
Uniform extensions of existing fixed-law fast-immigration asymptotics may already imply the stated joint crossover.
Novelty evaluation is a literature-dependent best-knowledge self-review, not independent validation.

value.rationale: The asymptotic cutoff is a natural design question: does ever-faster recruitment overcome simultaneously increasing searcher death? The theorem establishes the exact squared-logarithmic mortality boundary, resolves an extreme-arrival-to-success-waiting change of stochastic universality class, gives its finite critical window, and quantifies the nontrivial five-halves log-log centering. These facts describe a motivated parameter regime not a contrived finite invariant.
